title: Recording: I Lie Around by Wings; Now Hear This Song Of Mine by Paul and Linda McCartney | 1971
content:
Studio B, Sound Recorders Studio, Los Angeles
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Eirik Wangberg

The final studio session for the Ram album by Paul and Linda McCartney took place on 9 April 1971.

The last set of overdubs were added to ‘I Lie Around’. Paul recorded several vocal lines and an additional guitar part. Although considered at this stage to be a McCartney song, it was eventually released in June 1973 as the b-side of Wings’ ‘Live And Let Die’ single.

Attentions then turned to ‘Now Hear This Song Of Mine’, an experimental piece which was to be used in radio promotions for Ram. Work had previously taken place on 22 February and 1 March 1971.

During this session the McCartneys were recorded answered questions from studio engineer Eirik Wangberg, who was in the control room. They then assembled various radio spots, including snippets of the song, excerpts from the album, animal noises, and other sound effects.

The results were issued to radio stations on a promotional 12″ disc, titled Brung To Ewe By. The tracks, each lasting 30-60 seconds, were: ‘Get It Together Man’, ‘On A Fishing Boat’, ‘You Know What I Mean’, ‘Ram Ram… Boogie’, ‘Rama Rama…’, ‘We’ve Got To Get This Album Together Man’, ‘Snatch Of Uncle Albert’, ‘Snatch Of Ram On’, ‘Ram With Sounds Of Sheep’, ‘Ram On And Sheep Noises’, ‘On A Fishing Boat’, ‘Ram Ram’, ‘What Is This, Paul: This Is Work Woman’, ‘Paul Rambling In Scottish Accent’, ‘Very Short Clips Of Tracks’, and ‘Please Don’t Bring My Banjo Back’.
